subject: AR effects specific to members of a group

messages.author: 5063972801d34964
messages.subject: AR effects specific to members of a group
parts:
I am struggling to find the best way to specify an autoregressive effect focused on members of a group relative to time.

Assume we have a number of subjects ("ID") who are measured repeatedly (the "Reading") over a period of several days ("Days").  

Readings for each subject are expected to be correlated.  Readings for each subject on various days, including but possibly not limited to more recent days, are also expected to be correlated. Overall mean readings between recent days regardless of subject may also be correlated. There are no spatial effects.

Options include:

Random intercepts for all

inla(Reading ~ f(ID, model="iid") + f(Days, model="iid")

Random intercept for subject, random walk for time

inla(Reading ~ f(ID, model="iid") + f(Days, model="rw2")

Random intercept for subject, Ar1 for time

inla(Reading ~ f(ID, model="iid") + f(Days, model="ar1")

But how do we model the recency information specific to measurements of various IDs?
We could create a nested model with a separately-created interaction variable, which would capture at least some of this information, but would not distinguish days by recency:

Nested Model, one for each ID and Day

inla(Reading ~ f(ID, model="iid") + f(Days, model="ar1") + f(ID_Day, model="iid")

We could also make the interaction variable itself autoregressive, taking advantage of the fact that the ID_Day variable, if simply pasted from those two columns, will have some consecutive nature to it for each ID, albeit perhaps messy at the boundaries between IDs:

Nested Model, one for each ID and Day, AR1 effect

inla(Reading ~ f(ID, model="iid") + f(Days, model="ar1") + f(ID_Day, model="ar1")

From what I can see, the nested model can help a fair amount, and the nested with the Ar1 effect on the interaction variable can help slightly more.  But neither seems to specify recency limited only to particular IDs, or to reflect the fact that particular IDs may have their own unique recency effect over time, in addition to whatever recency effect the average group member has.
I suspect there is a way to specify an (additional) AR1 effect solely on Days within individual IDs, but I am struggling to identify it.  Perhaps the replicate or copy commands are needed? 

I have noticed ia "group" command within the "f" function, but I got an error when I tried to use it.  I'm not sure if that is because the IDs need to be consecutive or because this argument has nothing to do with what I am trying to accomplish.

I'd appreciate any insight. Thanks.

messages.author: 5063972801d34964
messages.subject: RE: AR effects specific to members of a group
parts:
It looks like the answer indeed is to use replicate.  For the example below, create a replicate version of the ID variable with its own index and then use that to introduce the AR1 term.  So:

 

Idx.repl <- seq_along(unique(ID))

 

inla(Reading ~ f(ID, model=”iid”) + Days + f(ID.repl, model=”ar1”, replicate=Days)

 

Checked an analogous model in glmmTMBB and got comparable results with this:

 

glmmTMB(Reading ~ (1|ID) + Days + ar1( Days + 0 | batter))

 

Jonathan
